name: Action menu
summary: A More button with its dropdown shown open: grouped actions with icons and shortcuts, a submenu, a disabled item and a danger action at the end. Positioning is the project's.
use: when a row or record has more actions than fit as buttons
a11y: A menu button with aria-expanded; items are menuitems with roving focus (arrow keys, Home, End), Escape closes and returns focus to the button, and the disabled item is aria-disabled.

use_when: a toolbar or card header where rare or destructive actions should stay out of sight until asked for
avoid_when: searching across many commands or pages by typing: use command-menu
only one or two actions: show them as buttons
an action that needs a reason or a second look before it runs: open confirm-dialog from the menu item

parts.name: trigger
parts.what: the More button that opens and closes the menu

parts.name: group
parts.what: a small heading over a group of items

parts.name: items
parts.what: one action: icon, label, then a shortcut, a submenu arrow or a note

parts.name: shortcut
parts.what: the key or keys shown for an item

parts.name: note
parts.what: why a disabled item is off

parts.name: danger
parts.what: the destructive action, last and in red

empty.how: the Smart UI renderer puts one plain 'Nothing to show yet.' line in an empty list

loading.how: the Smart UI renderer draws each marked slot as a quiet block of its size while the data arrives; the static file shows the filled part

error.how: if an action fails after the menu closes, report it with toast-stack

disabled.how: an item marked aria-disabled turns grey, shows a note on why, and clicking it does nothing

overflow.how: the menu has no height limit; for long lists give the menu a max height with its own scroll

long_text.how: a long label wraps in its column while shortcuts and notes stay on one line

keyboard: Enter or Space on More opens or closes the menu and focuses the first item
Arrow Down or Arrow Up on More opens the menu at the first or last item
Arrow Down and Arrow Up move between items and wrap around; Home and End jump to the first and last
Enter or Space runs the focused item and closes the menu, except the disabled item and Move to
Escape or Tab closes the menu and returns focus to More
the shortcut keys shown are labels only; the file does not listen for them
